_status: PLACEHOLDER -- schema NOT established; also sits on an OPEN SCOPE QUESTION
_read_this_first: NOTHING BELOW IS INVENTED. The keys in this file all begin with _ and are prose, not configuration. No field of the real schema is reproduced here, because no artifact in this repository shows one -- and a plausible-looking invented schema is worse than an acknowledged gap, because the next person builds against it.
_this_will_not_start_the_router: This file will NOT satisfy the application. It exists so that `docker compose up` has a real file to bind-mount -- Docker silently CREATES AN EMPTY DIRECTORY at a missing bind source, which would mount a directory onto /app/bifrost_shell_policy.json and fail as IsADirectoryError far from its cause. Replace the whole object when step 4 of RELEASE-SCOPE.md lands the source that reads it.
_established_from_this_repository: Mounted read-only at /app/bifrost_shell_policy.json -- deploy/compose.yaml mounts it as a single FILE, not as a directory, because a directory mounted onto /app would shadow the application code.
Read by the application as Path(__file__).parent / "bifrost_shell_policy.json", so it must land at that exact path (deploy/compose.yaml, deploy/README.md).

Absent from the router build context by design: deploy/images/router/.dockerignore does not re-admit it, and deploy/images/router/Dockerfile note 1 records that the private original baked all four in and the release cannot.
_scope_flag: Before this file is filled in, settle the scope question. RELEASE-SCOPE.md records docker/shell-mcp/ (6 paths) as a LIVE CONTRADICTION: the cut list names 'the agent sandbox' by name and the allowlist census selected those paths anyway. John's ruling of 2026-10-27 covered the portal and autopilot and did NOT extend to it. A shell policy is plausibly the configuration surface of exactly that family. The mount is already in the committed deploy/compose.yaml, so a file has to exist for the stack to start -- which is why this placeholder is here -- but deriving a real schema for it would be deciding the open question by implementation.
_not_established: Every key, value and nesting. The repository names the file and mounts it; nothing else.

What it governs. 'Bifrost' is the pre-release name of this system -- it survives in shared/resolver.py's compatibility aliases (BIFROST_ROUTER_BASE, BIFROST_KB_URL and the rest) and in the portal's BIFROST_HOST -- and bifrost_delegate.py gates every delegated leaf of the tool loop. Reading 'a policy over what delegated shell work may do' out of those two facts is INFERENCE, not evidence, and it is recorded here as inference.

Whether this file is fail-open or fail-closed when absent or unparseable. That matters more here than for the other three: deploy/images/router/Dockerfile and deploy/README.md both record that the delegation path fails CLOSED and silently while /health still answers 200, so a policy file that degrades quietly would be invisible in exactly the same way.
_placeholder_rules_for_whoever_fills_thi: Addresses: documentation range only -- 192.0.2.0/24 (RFC 5737 TEST-NET-1), or a name under example.com / example.invalid. Never a private address (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16) and never a host name from the private deployment.
Never a credential, key, token or password, not even a placeholder shaped like one. If a field appears to require a real secret, that is a finding, not a value to invent.
Keep the file LF-terminated and ASCII; .gitattributes normalises *.json to LF.
The operator's copy of this file (deploy/config/<name>.json, without .example) is ignored by .gitignore on purpose: it describes a specific fleet.
